sources.entry: Icecast 2 - Streaming audio/video server which can be used to create an Internet radio station or a privately running jukebox and many things in between. (Source Code, Clients) GPL-2.0 C

summary.name: Icecast
summary.one_liner: Icecast is a free, GPL-2.0 licensed streaming media (audio/video) server for running internet radio stations or private jukeboxes.
use_cases: Streaming audio to listeners over HTTP
Streaming video or Ogg Theora content
summary.what_it_does: Icecast is a streaming media server that supports Ogg (Vorbis and Theora), Opus, WebM and MP3 streams. It is used to create an internet radio station or a privately running jukebox. The page says new formats can be added relatively easily and that it supports open standards for communication and interaction. It includes a web interface, with the 2.5.0 release adding general web interface improvements and an experimental dark mode. The page also covers the 2.4.x end-of-support date and upgrade notes for 2.5.x.
notable: Supports Ogg Vorbis/Theora, Opus, WebM and MP3 streams
Reads Icecast 2.4.x configuration files in 2.5.x for seamless upgrades
Web interface with experimental dark mode in 2.5.0
caveats: Icecast 2.4.4 support ends 2026-12-31; only security fixes are accepted until then
2.5.0-rc2 release candidate was marked for production use with caution
